newsitem.title: BELGIUM: City Hotels to issue one bln Bfr bond.
newsitem.headline: City Hotels to issue one bln Bfr bond.

text.p: Belgian hotels and airline group City Hotels plans to issue a one billion Belgian franc bond with warrants in the next few weeks, chairman Victor Hasson said on Wednesday.
"It is (planned) for the coming weeks," Hasson told Reuters in an interview.
He declined to give any details of the loan but said it was not linked to City Hotels' new long-haul airline City Bird, which will be launched on March 27.
"It has nothing do do with the airline but with the development of our hotel business," Hasson said.

The airline, which has capital of $5 million, was already generating cash through charter flights from Paris. "The passengers pay regularly before the flights. At the cash level we don't need money," he said.
Hasson, who is also City Bird chairman, said City Hotels currently had about one billion francs ($29.4 million) in liquidity.
"We will borrow one billion so, we will have two billion available. But our goal is not to wolf down two billion in an airline. We would never do that," he said.
City Hotels has a 62.5-percent stake in the new airline, with the rest held by private investors.
